blocks.text:
City reaches agreement with Lyft, parent company of Citi Bike, in attempt to ‘make biking affordable for every New Yorker’

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, announced on Monday that the city has reached an agreement with Lyft, the parent company of Citi Bike, the city’s bike-share system, to cap ebike fares for members at $3.65 for rides of up to 45 mins, starting in mid-January.

In a video announcing the changes, the mayor’s office said that a 45-minute ebike ride currently costs members $12.15, but that under the new agreement, that price will fall to $3.65 from 19 January 2027.
